root_cause.text: In `fs/proc/task_mmu.c::do_procmap_query()`, the error path for an undersized build-ID buffer still jumped to the generic `out` label after `mmput(mm)` had already been executed earlier, causing a second `mmput()` on the same `mm_struct` due to the changed cleanup ordering introduced by the VMA-lock build-ID fetch refactor.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `goto out;` to `goto out_file;` for `-ENAMETOOLONG`, and the commit message explicitly says the condition now happens “after we unlocked mmap_lock/per-VMA lock and did mmput(), so original goto out is now wrong and will double-mmput() mm_struct,” with `out:` containing `query_vma_teardown(&lock_ctx); mmput(mm);` and `out_file:` only cleaning `vm_file` and `name_buf`.

Author: Andrii Nakryiko <andrii@kernel.org>

    procfs: avoid fetching build ID while holding VMA lock
    
    Fix PROCMAP_QUERY to fetch optional build ID only after dropping mmap_lock
    or per-VMA lock, whichever was used to lock VMA under question, to avoid
    deadlock reported by syzbot:
    
     -> #1 (&mm->mmap_lock){++++}-{4:4}:
            __might_fault+0xed/0x170
            _copy_to_iter+0x118/
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body does not contain the vulnerable construct anymore. The build-ID lookup was moved to after teardown: it now does `if (karg.build_id_size && vma->vm_file) vm_file = get_file(vma->vm_file);`, then `query_vma_teardown(&lock_ctx); mmput(mm);`, and only after that calls `build_id_parse_file(vm_file, build_id_buf, &build_id_sz)`. The previous buggy pattern is absent: the old code that did `build_id_parse(vma, ...)` under the VMA lock and then on undersized buffer `err = -ENAMETOOLONG; goto out;` is removed. Also, the cleanup label now safely handles `vm_file` with `if (vm_file) fput(vm_file);`, so this version already contains the fix and does not show the double-`mmput()` error path described.
